bib.title: Pretrained Transformers Improve Out-of-Distribution Robustness
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2020), pages 2744-2751

read.skipped: Nothing skipped. The PDF is the 8-page main paper only; the Appendix with full results that the text refers to is not in the file.

question: Do pretrained Transformers such as BERT generalize to out-of-distribution data and detect OOD examples better than earlier NLP models?
hypothesis: Implied: high IID accuracy may not translate to OOD robustness for pretrained Transformers, as in vision, so this is tested rather than assumed.
contributions: A new OOD robustness benchmark over seven NLP datasets with realistic distribution shifts (style, topic, vocabulary)
Evidence that pretrained Transformers have smaller IID/OOD gaps and detect OOD examples better than BoW, ConvNet and LSTM models
Analysis of factors: larger models are not necessarily more robust, distillation can hurt, more diverse pretraining data helps

method.summary: Thirteen models (bag-of-words, word-embedding encoders, pretrained Transformers) are trained on one distribution and tested on another, built by splitting datasets by metadata or pairing similar datasets. OOD generalization is the IID-to-OOD accuracy gap. OOD detection uses negative max softmax probability from an SST-2 classifier, scored by FAR95.
method.task: OOD generalization and OOD detection across sentiment analysis, textual entailment, reading comprehension and semantic similarity

datasets.name: SST-2 / IMDb
datasets.split: train on one, test on the other, and vice versa
datasets.source: Socher et al. 2013; Maas et al. 2011

datasets.name: Yelp Review Dataset
datasets.split: four groups by food type: American, Chinese, Italian, Japanese

datasets.name: Amazon Review Dataset
datasets.split: seven categories: Clothes, Women Clothing, Men Clothing, Baby Clothing, Shoes, Music, Movies
datasets.source: McAuley et al. 2015; He and McAuley 2016

datasets.name: STS-B
datasets.split: four sources from two genres: MSRpar, Headlines (news); MSRvid, Images (captions)

datasets.name: 20 Newsgroups, Multi30K, RTE, SNLI, WMT16 (English-German source side)
datasets.split: validation examples; RTE/SNLI use premise+hypothesis concatenated; used only as OOD examples for detection, never for training
datasets.source: Lang 1995; Elliott et al. 2016; Dagan et al. 2005; Bowman et al. 2015

models.name: Bag-of-words
models.architecture: BoW (used for sentiment and STS-B only)

models.name: word2vec / GloVe with averages, LSTM or ConvNet encoders (+MLP head); DocQA with GloVe for ReCoRD
RoBERTa Large
models.architecture: pretrained on a larger dataset than BERT

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning on each task's training distribution (standard BERT fine-tuning procedure)

other.hyperparameter_tuning: non-pretrained models tuned to maximize validation performance on the IID task; Transformers 'lightly tune the hyperparameters'

parameters.ood_detection_score: anomaly score = -max_y p(y|x), negative prediction confidence (maximum softmax probability)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy for sentiment, Amazon (5-way), MNLI

metrics.name: FAR95
metrics.definition: False Alarm Rate at 95% Recall: probability that an in-distribution example raises a false alarm, assuming 95% of OOD examples are detected

eval.protocol: Train on IID split, test on IID and OOD splits; gap between them is generalization. No seeds, repeats or significance tests stated. Full results are in an Appendix not included in this PDF.

results.claim: On STS-B (IID Images vs OOD MSRvid), an LSTM word2vec model's performance falls by over 35% while RoBERTa's slightly increases.
results.setup: STS-B, train Images test MSRvid, LSTM word2vec vs RoBERTa Large, read from Fig 1
results.quote: the LSTM model declined by over 35%
results.note: Abstract-level intro text says 'declines by over 35%' for an LSTM semantic similarity model.

results.claim: A BERT Base MNLI model trained on Telephone data keeps similar accuracy on OOD genres.
results.setup: MNLI, BERT Base trained on Telephone
results.table: Table 1, row BERT, columns Telephone (IID) 81.4%, Letters (OOD) 82.3%, Face-to-Face (OOD) 80.8%

results.claim: Larger BERT and ALBERT models do not shrink the IID/OOD gap on SST-2 vs IMDb, unlike in computer vision.
results.setup: BERT base/large and ALBERT base to xxlarge, train IMDb test SST-2 (Fig 3, no numbers in text)
results.quote: Figure 3 shows that larger BERT and AL-
results.note: Claim only; values are in the figure.

results.claim: Distillation can reduce robustness (DistilBERT worse OOD than BERT).
results.setup: ReCoRD and IMDb, DistilBERT vs BERT, Fig 2
results.quote: model distillation can reduce robustness, as evident

results.claim: More diverse and larger pretraining data (RoBERTa vs BERT Large) improves robustness, but data volume is not a full explanation.
results.note: Authors note BERT is pretrained on roughly 3 billion tokens while GloVe is trained on roughly 840 billion tokens, so data size alone does not explain robustness.

results.claim: Non-pretrained models are near or worse than chance at OOD detection, with false alarm rates approximately 100% on 20 Newsgroups.
results.setup: SST-2 classifiers (BoW, word2vec averages, LSTM, ConvNet) with max-softmax score, OOD set 20 Newsgroups
results.quote: as their false alarm rates are approximately 100%

results.claim: Pretrained Transformers always beat a random detector on FAR95 but still do not cleanly separate IID from OOD.
results.setup: SST-2 classifiers, OOD sets 20 NG, Multi30K, RTE, SNLI, WMT16
results.note: Numbers only in Fig 4 and the Appendix.

limits: The benchmark covers only classification, entailment, QA and similarity models of 2020 scale (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT); no generative or autoregressive LMs are tested.
Authors say why pretrained models are more robust is open; data diversity and self-supervision are only partial explanations.
OOD detection by max softmax probability is far from perfect for pretrained Transformers (Fig 5).
Hyperparameters, seeds, dataset sizes and per-dataset numbers are not in the main text; the Appendix is missing from this PDF.
Shifts studied are natural (style, topic, vocabulary), not adversarial; domain adaptation is excluded.

terms.definition: the False Alarm Rate at 95% Recall: the probability that an in-distribution example raises a false alarm, assuming that 95% of all out-of-distribution examples are detected
decomposed into a model's ability to (1) generalize and to (2) detect OOD examples
